acceptance: tpcds and tpcds_obt below 0.01 raise ScaleFactorOutOfRangeError, shown by a test that fails before the change.
The message states what was observed and makes no wider claim.
description:
## Problem
After #4335 and #4401, `validate_scale_factor` in benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.py calls `validate_tpcds_scale` first for a tpcds or tpcds_obt scale between 0 and the 0.01 floor, so the caller gets a plain `ValueError` instead of `ScaleFactorOutOfRangeError`. The message in benchbox/core/tpcds/compliance.py says dsdgen "does not finish below this scale"; the evidence is one run at SF 0.001 on darwin-arm64 killed after 60 s.

## Owner decision
Question: what #4401 left behind. Answer: "Recommended: raise ScaleFactorOutOfRangeError again, carrying the reason. Reword to what was observed: 'dsdgen did not finish at SF 0.001'." Source: owner's answer in the choice dialog, 2026-11-20.

## Change
`ScaleFactorOutOfRangeError` (an exported error) gains an optional `reason` that is appended to its message and kept as an attribute. `validate_scale_factor` raises it with the TPC-DS reason for a tpcds or tpcds_obt scale between 0 and the floor; this covers the CLI, MCP and the benchmark loader. Direct construction of the TPC-DS classes calls `validate_tpcds_scale` (benchbox/core/tpcds/benchmark/runner.py, tpcds/generator/manager.py, tpcds_obt/benchmark.py), which raised `ValueError` before #4335 and still does; only its wording changes. Reword the reason to the observation. The 0.01 floor is the owner's (2026-11-11: "Just raise the floor to 0.01 everywhere") and does not change.

## Decision gates
None. The floor value and the accepted range do not change.

## Verification rubric
Pass: a test fails on develop and passes after, showing `validate_scale_factor` for tpcds and tpcds_obt at 0.001 raises `ScaleFactorOutOfRangeError` whose text names the range and the observation and whose `reason` is set; a range error for another cause carries no reason; the CLI dry run and the MCP validation name the floor; the direct-construction path still raises `ValueError` with the reworded text; a changelog fragment describes the user-visible change.


## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
Accepted by the owner in the choice dialog: the agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. It arms with `make pr-arm` once per pull request and reports the result. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed. A blocked step stops this item; the agent moves to the next item and does not work around the block.
Review threads: the accepted text also said the agent never resolves a thread. Asked afterwards which rule applies, the owner chose: "The morning rule: I may resolve a thread once the bot has reviewed the new head and did not raise the finding again." ('I' is the agent.) So the agent pushes the fix and replies, and resolves a thread only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise that finding again.
